title: Streaming scratchpad — connection throttle & chunk delay repro
content:
Context:
I was running quick smoke tests against the public streaming endpoint and hit another case of delayed/throttled chunk delivery. Behavior differs between local dev (straight node server) and staging behind the ELB/ingress. Notes below capture commands tried, logs, hypotheses, and next experiments. This is a scratchpad — messy and chronological.

Environment:
- Client: macOS 13.6.2, curl 8.3.1, Node 20.1 (native fetch/EventSource tests)
- Server: staging cluster (k8s) behind AWS ALB -> NGINX ingress -> service -> pod (node/express streaming adapter).
- Observed when: hitting /v1/streams/chat (SSE) for call that streams tokens.

Observed symptoms (staging):
- After initial 1–2 small SSE events, the connection seems idle for 6–18s, then emits a burst of 8–20 events in quick succession.
- client shows RTTs stable; connection stays open (no 4xx/5xx) until final response completes.
- sometimes connection resets mid-stream with error: "write EPIPE" on the pod logs and client sees "error: socket hang up".
- curl --no-buffer shows chunk grouping (i.e., server flush doesn't reach client until after pause).

Quick repro commands tried:
1) Basic curl SSE (staging):
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=small-test"

Notes: curl -N and --no-buffer behave similarly; verbose shows single TCP conn, no additional connect attempts. Data arrives in groups after pause.

2) Local dev (direct pod port-forward) — behaves smoothly (no burst):
# port forward to pod and hit same route
akas kubectl port-forward svc/streaming-service 8080:8080 &
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/chat?model=small-test

3) Node client (EventSource polyfill):
// minimal client to subscribe
import EventSource from 'eventsource';
const es = new EventSource('https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=small-test', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer '+process.env.T } });
es.onmessage = e => console.log('m:', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.error('err', e);

Result: same bursty arrival pattern as curl.

4) curl with HTTP/2 forced/off:
# force HTTP/1.1 (some ALBs negotiate h2 by default)
curl --http1.1 -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=small-test
# force http2
curl --http2 -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=small-test

Result: behavior persisted under both; slightly more pronounced burstiness with http2=false. Not definitive.

Server-side logs snippets (staging pod):
[2026-02-12T15:02:02.213Z] request-id=abc123 route=/v1/streams/chat client=10.0.4.12 start_streaming
[2026-02-12T15:02:02.240Z] token-gen: sent-event token="▁Hello"
[2026-02-12T15:02:02.240Z] token-gen: sent-event token="▁world"
[2026-02-12T15:02:09.645Z] backpressure: paused=true queue_len=12 policy=adaptive
[2026-02-12T15:02:09.646Z] token-gen: produced 12 tokens (queued)
[2026-02-12T15:02:09.890Z] stream: flush->write 12 events
[2026-02-12T15:02:09.891Z] http: write 12 events (nwrite 2048)
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.002Z] network: tls record written size=16384
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.008Z] request-id=abc123 end_streaming

Interpretation of logs: runtime enqueues tokens while backpressure=true, then a flush happens which writes many events at once. The timing aligns with the pause seen on the client. But why is backpressure=true in staging and not in local port-forward? Potential choke points: ALB/NGINX buffering, TLS record coalescing, default socket write buffering at cluster egress, or our runtime's buffer-pressure heuristics incorrectly triggering when egress rate is limited.

Commands/headers attempted to disable buffering along the path:
- curl with --no-buffer (client side) -> no change.
- Set header X-Accel-Buffering: no in upstream (NGINX) config for the streaming route (temporary change) -> results improved (fewer big bursts) in manual test.
- Added header Transfer-Encoding: chunked explicitly from backend -> no visible change (probably already chunked).
- Added header Connection: keep-alive with no effect.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NGINX/ingress buffering: by default some NGINX configs buffer proxy responses and only flush on certain sizes/timeouts; adding X-Accel-Buffering: no reduces buffering. Local port-forward bypasses ingress so smooth. Strong candidate.
2) ALB or AWS network-level batching: ALB may coalesce small writes especially when TLS is used with certain TLS record sizes. But changing to http/1.1 did not eliminate behavior. Medium likelihood.
3) Our runtime's dynamic backpressure threshold miscalibrated for the staging egress profile. It sets paused=true when send queue > 8 and only flushes every 200ms; local test has lower latency and doesn't hit threshold. Medium-high likelihood.
4) Client TCP stack coalescing on macOS (Nagle) — unlikely since curl --no-buffer and EventSource both show same pattern. Low likelihood.

Repro tests to run (next):
1) Controlled NGINX experiment: temporarily route traffic from a test ingress with proxy_buffering off and compare. (We did a quick test — better but need reproducible A/B).
2) Instrument runtime to log bytes written per syscall and time between syscalls (so we can tell whether runtime flushes in many small syscalls or batches into fewer larger writes). Add trace header X-Debug-Stream: true to correlate.
3) Stress test with artificial egress throttle (tc qdisc) on pod to reproduce pause locally:
# inside container (minikube/test pod)
apt-get update && apt-get install -y iproute2
 tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 200kbps burst 32k latency 400ms
# then run same stream and observe if backpressure triggers earlier

4) Minimal Node repro (local) to emulate streaming code path:
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, {
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
    Connection: 'keep-alive',
  });
  let i = 0;
  const iv = setInterval(() => {
    i += 1;
    res.write(`data: token-${i}\n\n`);
    // purposely do NOT flush/res.flush() in this minimal server
    if (i === 30) { clearInterval(iv); res.end(); }
  }, 100);
}).listen(9000);

# then try via proxy ingress and direct to see delta

Notes from quick experiments so far:
- Adding X-Accel-Buffering: no at ingress layer materially reduced the pause (client saw more even spacing) — points to ingress buffering being a big factor.
- tbf on pod egress reproduced burstiness even locally (good signal that egress throughput constraints + runtime backpressure combine to create batching).

Potential fixes to test in staging (canary):
- Set proxy_buffering off for streaming paths in NGINX ingress config, and add X-Accel-Buffering: no as header from upstream. Monitor CPU/throughput implications (buffering off increases memory churn).
- Adjust runtime policy: lower the pause threshold, flush more frequently under small-queue conditions (e.g., if queue_len < 32 flush immediately), or add an adaptive flush timer that triggers sooner on long idle periods.
- Tune ALB idle/keepalive/write timeouts if ALB is coalescing writes (ops coordination).

Short-term mitigation: use header to disable buffering at ingress for customer-facing streaming routes; follow with runtime tweak to reduce queueing window.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there customers still seeing chunking/burst issues behind some cloud providers' load balancers? Ask SRE/infra to list differences between staging vs prod ALB configs.
- Add a small synthetic test job that runs every 5m and measures inter-event latency distribution for streaming endpoints to detect regressions automatically.
- Confirm TLS record sizes with packet capture to see whether coalescing happens at TLS layer. Need Ops signoff to capture pcap in staging.

Raw error snippets noticed on pods:
- runtime: write EPIPE at StreamWriter._write (/app/dist/stream-writer.js:88:15)
- http: socket hang up (client aborted)
- ingress-controller: upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream

Notes-to-self: when filing a follow-up ticket, attach: (1) curl traces -v for both local and staging, (2) ingress config diff showing proxy_buffering toggle, (3) runtime debug logs with X-Debug-Stream correlation id, (4) tc qdisc recipe used for local repro.

End summary (one-liner): ingress buffering + runtime backpressure interaction appears to be the root cause; temporary fix is to disable proxy buffering for streaming routes and tune runtime flush policy.

-- Avery
